plan.title: After onboarding, the coach talks from the full voice page

transcript.text: Hey! I'm Riley, I want to read every day

Hey Riley, I'm ZOH! I'll help you get better at one thing, with a small step each day. Text "stop" anytime, and tell me whenever you want me to coach differently, like "chill out" or "push me harder". Reading every day? Let's go! What are you into reading right now, or is there a book or topic you've been meaning to get to?
mostly fantasy, I read on my phone on the train
Fantasy on the train, that's a great daily setup. What time is your train, the one you'd read on?
Perfect, 20 minutes on the 8 am train. Which fantasy book are you reading right now, or do you want to start a new one?

No problem, Riley, we'll keep it simple. Is there somewhere you want this daily reading to get you? That could be finishing a series, a book a month, or just making it a habit. "Not sure yet" is a fine answer too.
Got it, fewer emojis from here on. Back to the plan: is there somewhere you want this reading to take you, like finishing a series or a book a month? "Not sure yet" works too.
honestly is 20 min even worth it?

Yes, 20 minutes is worth it. At an average pace that's about 5,000 words a day, so a typical fantasy novel takes you roughly three to four weeks. Over a year that's a dozen or so books, and doing it daily is what makes it stick. If it ever feels too small, we can bump it up. Would finishing a book every month or so feel like a good target, or do you want to skip the target for now?

Riley, a book a month fits what you've told me: 20 minutes on your phone, on the train. Here's the plan:

• Headed for: about a book a month
• Tonight (day 1): read 20 minutes of a fantasy book on your phone, anywhere you like, done by 9 pm. Pick your book now if you haven't started one.
• Usual: 8 am on the train, 20 minutes, every day
• Proof: a short voice note recapping what you read, in your words. It helps the story stick. If you'd rather, a screenshot of the page you stopped on works too.
• I'll text you a heads-up at 7:50 am so I reach you before the train.

Each day shapes the next step, so we can nudge it up if 20 minutes starts to feel easy. What do you think?

grade.summary: ZOH stayed on track through onboarding, applied the no-emoji request cleanly, and moved into the plan without a recap line. Its weak spots are the invented reading-pace statistics in the answer about 20 minutes and a plan that treats the ambiguous 'lol ok' as a firm yes to a book a month.
